snippet.title: Scotland's Witch Trials | Witches: Truth Behind the Trials | National Geographic UK
snippet.description:
While the Salem witch trials may be the most well-known, witch trials took place all over the world in the 15th - 18th centuries. Scotland's first witch trials took place when storms threatened the sinking of ships carrying King James VI of Scotland and his future wife. Blame focussed on so-called witches, sparking a determination in the King to hunt, torture and eliminate them.

snippet.title: The Salem Witch Trials – The Real Locations  | American History (No AI Documentary)
snippet.description:
In 1692, the Salem Witch Trials tore apart an entire community — yet many of the most important locations connected to the accusations, examinations, and executions were lost to history.

In this episode of The History Explorer, we go beyond the museums and myths to physically visit the real, long-forgotten sites of Salem Witchcraft, many of which have only recently been rediscovered or correctly identified through modern scholarship, land records, and archaeological research.

This is not the Salem of Halloween folklore.
This is the actual landscape of fear, paranoia, and injustice.

We walk the ground where accusations were first made, examine the true locations of homes, meeting houses, and gallows sites, and explain why these places disappeared from public memory for over three centuries. Using period maps, contemporary accounts, and modern field investigation, this video reconstructs how Salem Village (modern Danvers) and Salem Town became the epicentre of one of history’s most infamous miscarriages of justice.

But if you confess, apologize, and implicate others, you’ll go free. This was the choice facing those accused of witchcraft in Salem, Massachusetts in the 17th century. How did this happen? Brian A. Pavlac investigates.

snippet.title: Why Witch Hunts are not just a Dark Chapter from the Past
snippet.description:
Whether in Macbeth, Harry Potter or Hansel and Gretel – witches have a long tradition in literature and film, often celebrated as strong, independent women, or portrayed as the incarnation of evil. But in a recent global study, over 40 percent of those surveyed said they believe in malevolent witchcraft. So witches are not just the stuff of fantasy nor a phenomenon of some distant medieval past.

As the descendant of a family that lost several members to witch hunts, DW-reporter Karin Helmstaedt goes searching for clues, speaking to experts and digging through archives in southern Germany. From the beginning of the Great European Witch Hunts in the 15th century to witch hunts in present-day Africa and Asia, this episode of Arts Unveiled goes after the truth about why they really happened, and why being singled out as a witch can still be deadly today.

snippet.title: Witch Hunt In Salem: Historical Retelling of the Famous Trials | Retold
snippet.description:
New England, 1692: religious hysteria infects the people of small-town Salem and brings about a ruthless manhunt. At a time when Europe has largely overcome the witch craze, dozens of people are accused of sorcery and executed. It is the puritans’ fall from grace, which ends their profound influence in the new world.

To this day, the case of Salem fascinates scholars and artists alike since the cause of the collective mania remains a mystery. Competing theories name a combination of religious hysteria, aggressively suppressed sexuality, the fear of the “devilish Indians”, common avarice, and the dual worldview of the puritans. In their highly religious society the visible world is just as real as an invisible parallel sphere inhabited by God, but also the devil.

snippet.title: The Witch-Hunter King: James I's Crusade On Witchcraft | War on Witches | Timeline
snippet.description:
In the late 16th century Europe was in the grip of a witch hunt fever, where thousands were tortured and burnt at the stake. The church was fully behind this terrifying crusade. In France and Germany alone up to 40,000 people may have been killed as witches. But England and Scotland were almost untouched by witch persecutions until King James himself decided to launch his own, personal war on witchcraft.

In 1597 King James VI of Scotland published 'Daemonology', a handbook on how to recognise and destroy, witches. It fuelled waves of witch hunting throughout Britain.

This film explores how James's obsession fueled trials across the country, while revealing groundbreaking archaeological evidence from Cornwall that suggests witchcraft wasn’t just a paranoid myth, but a practice that survived in the shadows for centuries.

snippet.description:

The Pittenweem Witch Trials of the early 18th Century were among Scotland’s last notorious witch hunts. In the small fishing village of Pittenweem, Fife, several locals were accused of witchcraft after a teenage boy claimed they were responsible for his illness. The most infamous case was Janet Cornfoot, falsely accused of sorcery. She was brutally lynched by a mob—stoned, beaten, and crushed under heavy stones—while authorities turned a blind eye. Others accused endured torture, imprisonment, and public humiliation.

snippet.title: The True Story of Witches: Magic, Myth and Modern Practice | Documentary
snippet.description:
Witches and their ancient practices have always held us spellbound, from the first whispers of witchcraft to modern-day witches. Witchcraft fascinates us now more than ever, as we uncover how these powerful witches shaped our understanding of magic and ritual. Ancient magical traditions and archaeological findings reveal how practitioners influenced societies worldwide, challenging our perception of their role. Far from the devil-worshipping figures of folklore, these practitioners faced persecution driven by fear and prejudice. 

Modern magic continues to attract a new generation, particularly among young women who embrace these ancient practices. This Witch-Documentary uncovers the fascinating reality behind the myths - from historical witch hunts to the psychology of supernatural beliefs. By examining both historical records and contemporary magical practices, we reveal the complex legacy of those accused of witchcraft and explore why their stories still resonate so powerfully today.
